rundown: Italy beat Fiji 23-21 at Allianz Stadium in London, England. It was level at 0-0 at the half.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 27, 11:39 AM ET. It had Fiji 51% and Italy 49%, projecting Fiji 24.3 – Italy 24 (48.4 total, Fiji by 0.3).

Final: Fiji 21 – Italy 23. Wrong winner: it had Fiji at 51%, and Italy (49%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Fiji came in with a 21% below average attack and a 23% leakier than average defense (WLLWT, 17 scored and 43 allowed a game over 6 games), worth about 12 and 12 games of evidence. Projected to score 24.3, they scored 21 (−3.3 points, 14% under); projected to allow 24, they allowed 23 (−1 points, 4% under).

Italy came in with a 31% below average attack and a 21% leakier than average defense (LLLLL, 12.3 scored and 39.5 allowed a game over 6 games), worth about 13 and 13 games of evidence. Projected to score 24, they scored 23 (−1 points, 4% under); projected to allow 24.3, they allowed 21 (−3.3 points, 14% under).

The bigger miss was Fiji's scoring (-3.3 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations

Total: 44 against 48.4 projected (-4.4), about the 39th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15).

Margin: Italy by 2 against Fiji by 0.3 projected, about the 56th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±16).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.body: Form (FIJ 2-2 L5 · ITA 0-5 L5): Italy ×0.94, Fiji ×1.00. It favored Fiji, who did not beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (FIJ lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection landed within its normal range anyway, so the flags didn't cost it much this time.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.889 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +3.6 points. It counts toward Rugby scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 28 graded Rugby games the algo now scales scoring ×0.975 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: Fiji attack ×0.967, defense ×0.990 (4 games); Italy attack ×0.960, defense ×0.991 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
